title: Rigidity of isogenies on a torus and simple root groups
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G,H$ be reductive affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme], meaning smooth connected groups of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup; unipotent means unipotent geometric matrices in a faithful representation. Fix split maximal tori $T\subseteq G$, $S\subseteq H$, and a simple-root base $\Delta$ for the reduced root datum of $(G,T)$, as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Use the root subgroup schemes $U_\alpha\subseteq G$ of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. Suppose $f,g:G\to H$ are surjective group-scheme homomorphisms with finite scheme-theoretic kernels, where finite means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra, and both map $T$ into $S$ as scheme morphisms. If $f|_T=g|_T$ and $f|_{U_\alpha}=g|_{U_\alpha}$ for every $\alpha\in\Delta$, then $f=g$ as morphisms of group schemes. Every restriction equality is scheme-theoretic, equivalently on points over every commutative $F$-algebra. No separability or reducedness of the kernels is assumed, and $\Delta=\varnothing$ is allowed.

source.place: Corollary 21.63, printed p.443; proof via Proposition 17.21, printed p.358, on each rank-one subgroup and Proposition 21.62, printed p.443.

proof.text: Fix $\alpha\in\Delta$. In the finite free character lattice $X=X^*(T)$, apply [lem-sfb-pid-submodule-smith-bases] over $\mathbf Z$ to $\mathbf Z\alpha\subseteq X$. After a sign change this gives a basis $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_r$ with $\alpha=d\epsilon_1$, $d>0$. By [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality] these basis characters identify $T$ with $\mathbf G_m^r$. The largest subtorus $T_\alpha$ of $\ker\alpha$ is $\{t_1=1\}$: it is a subtorus in the kernel, and for any torus $L$ in that kernel, $d(\epsilon_1|_L)=0$ forces $\epsilon_1|_L=0$ because the character group of $L$ is free. Consequently a character of $T$ is trivial on $T_\alpha$ exactly when it lies in $\mathbf Q\alpha\cap X$. This retains the possibly nonreduced finite factor in $\ker\alpha$; it is not substituted for its largest subtorus.

source.place: Definition preceding Theorem 21.11, p.428; Theorem 12.9(a), pp.233--234. Character-coordinate expansion of the root-kernel torus.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], $G_\alpha=C_G(T_\alpha)$ is a reductive connected smooth closed subgroup. It contains $T$, which is maximal there because it is maximal in $G$. The defining commutation equations over dual numbers give $\operatorname{Lie}(G_\alpha)=\operatorname{Lie}(G)^{T_\alpha}$: a tangent vector centralizes the torus precisely when its conjugation action is fixed after every scalar extension. In the weight decomposition supplied by the same node, step 1 retains exactly the zero weight and weights in $\mathbf Q\alpha$. Reducedness supplied there leaves only $\alpha,-\alpha$. Thus the roots of $(G_\alpha,T)$ are exactly $\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$. The conjugation formula in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] puts $U_\alpha,U_{-\alpha}$ inside $G_\alpha$, since both characters are trivial on $T_\alpha$. Their tangent spaces are the respective weight spaces, so uniqueness in that node, applied to $G_\alpha$, identifies them with its own root subgroup schemes.

source.place: Theorem 21.11(a),(b), pp.428--429, including its tangent-invariants calculation; formula (135), p.431.

proof.text: Use the coroot $\lambda=\alpha^\vee:\mathbf G_m\to T$. Its pairings with the two roots of $G_\alpha$ are $2,-2$, so it is regular, including in characteristic two: these are integer character pairings. By [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description], $B_\alpha=P_{G_\alpha}(\lambda)$ is a Borel containing $T$ with positive root set $\{\alpha\}$. By [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] applied to $G_\alpha$ and this Borel, its unipotent radical is $U_\alpha$. The Borel splitting of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] therefore makes multiplication $U_\alpha\times_F T\to B_\alpha$ an isomorphism of schemes.

source.place: Proposition 21.29 and Theorem 21.32, pp.433--435; Theorem 21.68(a), p.445; Borel subgroup U_alpha T in the proof of Corollary 21.63, p.443.

proof.text: For every commutative $F$-algebra $R$, write a point of $B_\alpha(R)$ uniquely as $ut$ using step 3. Then $f(ut)=f(u)f(t)=g(u)g(t)=g(ut)$ by the two restriction hypotheses. Hence the two homomorphisms $f|_{G_\alpha},g|_{G_\alpha}:G_\alpha\to H$ agree on $B_\alpha$ as scheme morphisms. Apply [lem-sfb-homomorphism-borel-rigidity]: $G_\alpha$ is smooth connected affine of finite type by step 2, $H$ has those properties by hypothesis, and $B_\alpha$ is a Borel by step 3. It follows that the restrictions agree on $G_\alpha$, and therefore on $U_{-\alpha}$. This holds for every $\alpha\in\Delta$.

source.place: Proposition 17.21, p.358, applied as in the proof of Corollary 21.63, p.443.

proof.text: Let $E\subseteq G$ be the closed subscheme defined in $F[G]$ by all $f^*(a)-g^*(a)$ for $a\in F[H]$. For every $F$-algebra $R$ its points are exactly $\{x:f(x)=g(x)\}$. This set contains the identity and is closed under multiplication and inversion because $f,g$ are homomorphisms. Thus $E$ is a closed subgroup scheme by [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. It contains $T$ and each $U_\alpha,U_{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\in\Delta$, by hypothesis and step 4. The generation assertion of [lem-sfb-simple-root-generation-mixed-commutation] gives $E=G$, so $f=g$. If $\Delta$ is empty the same assertion gives $G=T$ and the torus equality already proves the result. The argument used all test algebras throughout and never imposed separability or reducedness on either kernel.

source.place: Proposition 21.62 and Corollary 21.63, p.443; closed equalizer argument spells out scheme-theoretic generation.

proof_origin.place: Corollary 21.63, printed p.443: Proposition 17.21 on each rank-one centralizer, followed by Proposition 21.62. Rank-one Borel geometry expanded using Theorem 21.11 and existing Borel product/regular-cocharacter nodes.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q36-d47f2389c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS, with no fixes. I read the item, the one new node and the statements of all ten cited nodes in full. I checked them against Milne Cor. 21.63 and Props. 17.21 and 21.62 (pp.358, 443). Milne proves 21.63 in one line: agreement on the Borel of each rank-one subgroup, then 17.21, then generation by 21.62. The five steps follow that proof. Step 1 uses the Smith-basis and character-antiduality nodes: with alpha=d*eps_1, the largest subtorus in ker alpha is {t1=1}. Step 2: the rank-one centralizer is reductive, its Lie algebra is the fixed part (proved directly with dual numbers), its roots are {+alpha,-alpha} because Q*alpha meets the roots only there, and U_{+-alpha} are its root subgroups by the uniqueness clause. Step 3: the coroot is regular since the pairings are +-2, which holds in every characteristic; P(lambda) is a Borel with positive roots {alpha}, and U_alpha x T -> B_alpha is an isomorphism. Step 4 applies the new 17.21 node to the restrictions of f and g to that rank-one subgroup. Step 5: the equalizer is a closed subgroup scheme, and the generation node gives E=G, including the case of an empty base. The new node lem-sfb-homomorphism-borel-rigidity is Milne 17.21 in the case R=k over an algebraically closed field. It has a statement only and is self-contained, with five recorded searches and the right blueprint fields. It does not duplicate an existing node: I searched with rg for 17.21 and read the Borel-related statements. It is not a clause of the item. Edge cases checked: empty base, Frobenius with a non-reduced kernel, and SL2 against PGL2 in characteristic 2. All cited statements are in the item's own unit, there is no cycle and no SGA source. Batch-5 check: the five flagged citations reach sec-trace-formula only through generic lemmas: exterior-power and dual base change, fpqc descent of smoothness, base change of fppf coverings, and freeness of finitely generated torsion-free abelian groups. None of these is part of the proof of the trace formula or of Poincare duality. Minor: the new node defines Borel inline instead of citing def-sfb-borel-subgroup-scheme; the definitions are equivalent, so I did not count this as a fault.
